newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus firm to import 150,000 T grain in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Belarus firm to import 150,000 T grain in 1997.

text.p: Belarus grain supplier Prodimport will import around 150,000 tonnes of food and feed grains in 1997, some of German origin, Interfax news agency quoted Prodimport general director Fedor Begansky as saying Thursday.
The imports would include 50,000 tonnes of food wheat, and some contracts had already been sealed for second-class soft wheat of German origin, he was quoted as saying.
Begansky said Prodimport planned to import 70,000 tonnes of feed grains from Russia and Ukraine in 1997, and 30,000 tonnes of soymeal.
A delivery of 4,000 tonnes of Argentinian soymeal was due to arrive in Belarus in late February or early March, he said.
Holding company Prodimport is the main grain supplier to processors of baked goods and feed grains in Belarus.
Belarus produced a net 5.79 million tonnes of grain in 1996, up from 5.60 million tonnes in 1995.
Interfax quoted analysts' estimates of grain demand in the former Soviet republic as slightly more than six million tonnes a year.
